value.body: Government hospitals, medical colleges, mental health institutes and the District Mental Health Programme employ psychologists to assess and treat patients. For posts titled clinical psychologist, the usual requirement is an RCI-recognised clinical psychology qualification — a two-year M.Phil in Clinical Psychology or a professional doctorate (PsyD) — plus registration with the Rehabilitation Council of India. A BA in Psychology is the first step, not the qualification for the post.

items.label: Legal definition
items.note: Defines a clinical psychologist by an RCI-recognised qualification

items.label: Typical path
items.value: BA → MA/M.Sc Psychology → M.Phil Clinical Psychology

items.label: RCI-registered clinical psychologists
items.note: A 2026 Indian Journal of Clinical Psychology analysis of the register reported ~3,900 (as reported); counts differ by method
items.source: Rajya Sabha reply, via data.gov.in (as reported)

items.label: Clinical psychologists in the country
items.note: Older official headcount, given alongside ~3,800 psychiatrists

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After a BA in Psychology, complete an MA or M.Sc in Psychology, then an RCI-recognised M.Phil in Clinical Psychology (or PsyD), and register with RCI. Posts are advertised by state health departments, central institutes and medical colleges, and under NHM for district mental health programmes — usually filled by interview or a written test.

value.title: At a glance
items: M.Phil Clinical Psychology seats are few, and entrance is competitive.
NEP 2020 phased out the general M.Phil, which has caused uncertainty about the clinical route; RCI's current rules decide what is accepted.
Counsellor and counselling-psychologist posts may accept an MA in Psychology without the M.Phil.
